name: Ligustrum

project_scope.native_range_note: All three are non-native comparison taxa; preserve species-level labels and exclude from confirmed-native counts.

look_here_first: At a twig node, find opposite simple leaves with entire margins. Compare mature leaf length and texture, then inspect the underside midvein for hairs. For small-leaved privets, use a macro to compare individual flower/fruit stalks rather than flower color.
shared_traits: Opposite or nearly opposite simple entire leaves on woody shrubs or trees
Small four-lobed flowers in branched clusters; typically two stamens
Dark drupes at maturity; fruit color alone does not separate species

comparison_matrix.L. lucidum: thick glossy, usually 7–15 cm; conspicuous opaque marginal rim
comparison_matrix.L. quihoui: narrow elliptic to oblanceolate, about 10–36 × 4–11 mm; strongly tapered base
blade largely glabrous; young axes often short-hairy
comparison_matrix.L. sinense: often hairy along lower midvein, petioles and young shoots

comparison_matrix.L. lucidum: large terminal branched panicles, often 13–20 cm
comparison_matrix.L. sinense: individual flowers/fruits more distinctly pedicelled; shorter panicles

comparison_matrix.L. quihoui: spreading, near-horizontal branchlets; smaller semi-evergreen shrub

quick_key.if: Mature leaves generally >7 cm, thick glossy with opaque rim; large terminal panicles
Small narrow leaves taper to very short petioles, near-horizontal branchlets, flowers/fruits nearly stalkless
Thinner broader leaves with hairs beneath along midvein, distinctly stalked flowers/fruits

cautions: Shade, pruning and juvenile shoots alter leaf size and architecture; sample multiple mature, unpruned shoots.
Quihoui versus Chinese privet requires flower/fruit pedicel close-ups when leaves overlap.
Hairs may be sparse or worn; inspect several lower midveins and petioles.
All three are introduced encounter taxa, not project confirmed natives.

lookalikes.difference: Yaupon leaves alternate and often crenate; Ligustrum leaves opposite and entire. Check several nodes.
Also thick glossy-leaved; compare leaf marginal rim, venation and reproductive structures before naming L. lucidum.
Also Oleaceae with opposite simple leaves and drupes, but flowers are small and often lack the conspicuous four-lobed Ligustrum corolla.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched same-scale mature leaf upper and lower surfaces for all three species
Node macro showing opposite leaf attachment and petiole lengths
L. lucidum: opaque marginal rim and 6–8 vein pairs with scale
L. quihoui versus L. sinense: paired underside midvein hair macros
L. quihoui versus L. sinense: matched flowering/fruiting branch macro with arrows to pedicels
Whole unpruned branch architecture and panicle size for all three
Ilex vomitoria alternate leaf nodes versus Ligustrum opposite nodes
